summary.short: 21 CFR § 870.2345 classifies over-the-counter electrocardiograph software devices, which create, analyze and display ECG data and can provide information for identifying cardiac arrhythmias, as Class II (special controls). The special controls require clinical, software, non-clinical and human-factors testing, and labeling for such devices.
summary.long: Section 870.2345 identifies an over-the-counter electrocardiograph software device as one that creates, analyzes and displays electrocardiograph data and can provide information for identifying cardiac arrhythmias, and states that it is not intended to provide a diagnosis. It classifies the device as Class II (special controls). The special controls require: (1) clinical performance testing under anticipated conditions of use, showing the ability to obtain an ECG of sufficient quality and the detection algorithm's sensitivity and either specificity or positive predictive value; (2) software verification, validation and hazard analysis, with documentation characterizing the software's technical specifications, detection algorithm and its inputs and outputs; (3) non-clinical performance testing of the detection algorithm against a previously adjudicated data set; (4) human factors and usability testing showing that users can use the device from its labeling alone, interpret its output and understand when to seek medical care; and (5) labeling covering hardware and operating system requirements, situations where the device may not perform at an expected level, a summary of clinical performance testing, a description of what the device measures and outputs, and guidance on interpreting results. The text states no effective date and contains no enforcement or penalty provisions. It does not use the terms artificial intelligence or machine learning.

obligations.summary: Special controls for the device require clinical performance testing under anticipated conditions of use, demonstrating image quality for analysis and detection-algorithm performance as sensitivity and either specificity or positive predictive value. The text also requires non-clinical testing of detection-algorithm performance on a previously adjudicated data set (b)(3) and human factors and usability testing (b)(4). The text does not name the addressee; the duties are stated for the device.
